claim_natural: Every elementary function that appears on a standard scientific calculator — including \(+\), \(\times\), \(\div\), exponentiation \(x^y\), \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\tan\), \(\sqrt{x}\), \(\log_{10}\), \(\pi\), \(e\), \(i\), and their compositions and inverses — can be realised as a finite binary tree of the operator \(\mathrm{eml}(a, b) = e^{a} - \ln b\) whose leaves are the constant \(1\) and the input variables. Each construction is verified to machine precision at multiple test points on its natural domain.
